q: A stream uses `trigger(processingTime="1 minute")`. Batch 5 starts at 10:05:00 and runs for 80 seconds. When does batch 6 start?
o: At 10:06:00, in parallel with batch 5
At 10:06:20, right after batch 5 ends
At 10:07:00, the next boundary after batch 5 ends
Two batches start at 10:06:20 to catch up
e: When a batch misses the next interval boundary, the next batch starts as soon as the late one finishes. Batches of one query never overlap, and missed intervals are not replayed.

q: 12 new files are waiting. You run `trigger(availableNow=True)` with `maxFilesPerTrigger = 5`. What happens?
o: One batch of 12 files, then the query stops
Three batches (5, 5 and 2 files), then the query stops
Three batches, then the query keeps waiting for new files
One batch of 5 files; the rest wait for the next run
e: availableNow processes everything that existed when it started, in as many batches as the size limits require, and then stops on its own.

q: Which trigger can a streaming query use on serverless compute?
o: `processingTime="10 seconds"`
No trigger (the default)
`availableNow=True`
`realTime="5 minutes"`
e: Serverless supports only `availableNow` (and the deprecated `once`). Always-on triggers need classic compute; real-time mode needs a dedicated classic cluster.

o: `once` is slower because it waits for the next interval
`once` ignores size limits such as `maxFilesPerTrigger` and builds one batch of everything
`once` does not write a checkpoint
`once` only works with Kafka
e: Both process the available data and stop, but `once` does it in a single batch. availableNow splits a large backlog into batches that respect the rate limits.

q: A report must be at most 30 minutes old. Which setup is usually the cheapest?
o: An always-on stream with the default trigger
`processingTime="30 minutes"` on an always-on cluster
A Lakeflow Job that runs the stream with `availableNow` every 15 minutes
Real-time mode with a 30-minute interval
e: This is incremental batch: the checkpoint still makes each run read only new data, but compute runs only during the job, and it works on serverless.
